appraisal_events.evidence: « Autant par politesse pour ses amis à qui les professions de foi dreyfusardes de Saint-Loup étaient pénibles que parce que le reste m'intéressait davantage, je demandai à mon voisin... »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator deliberately steers the conversation away from Saint-Loup, reporting that his Dreyfusard declarations are painful to his own friends and that the narrator himself found the other subject more interesting; Saint-Loup's speech is thus set aside as a social liability and he loses the floor to an unnamed neighbour.

appraisal_events.evidence: « si c'était exact que ce commandant fît, de l'histoire militaire, une démonstration d'une véritable beauté esthétique. — C'est absolument vrai », suivi de la comparaison du palimpseste et d'« un ensemble aussi intellectuel que n'importe quelle science ou n'importe quel art ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's neighbour confirms without reservation that the commandant makes military history into a demonstration of genuine aesthetic beauty, and elaborates the claim at length; the commandant is locally elevated as an intellectual and artistic authority.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup is locally lowered because his Dreyfusard professions are reported as an embarrassment to the very friends he is dining with, and the narrator must manage the discomfort by changing the subject.
Having held the floor in the preceding exchange, Saint-Loup is displaced: the narrator turns to a neighbour, who then dominates the conversation with the palimpsest exposition.
The absent commandant gains local standing: his teaching is endorsed as an intellectually and aesthetically serious achievement, on a par with any science or art.

ambiguities: The evaluator of the commandant is only « mon voisin », an unnamed member of Saint-Loup's circle who is not on the reference sheet; the praise therefore comes from an unidentified source rather than from a tracked character.

The diminishment of Saint-Loup is doubly mediated: the discomfort (« pénibles ») is attributed to his friends, while the narrator gives his own greater interest in the other topic as an equally weighted motive, so the turn reads as a tactful withdrawal of attention rather than an overt snub.
